claim: Kernel-checked output removes false positives: every accepted proof is correct by construction, so verify-by-checker is the strongest S8 signal available.
agent_test: Compare self-verify by LLM judge vs executable checker (code run, unit test) at equal tokens on tasks with a checkable form.

claim: A fine-tuned language model proposing steps or proofs beats classical automation alone on proof-assistant benchmarks (GPT-f 56.22 vs 21.16 on Metamath; PACT 32 to 48.4 on mathlib).
agent_test: Not testable without a formal checker; motivation only.

claim: Combining neural proposal with a symbolic tool beats either alone: Thor 39.0 to 57.0 on PISA (union of LM and Sledgehammer only 48.8); Baldur+Thor 65.7 vs Thor 58.0; Cobblestone 48 vs 30 for Proverbot9001.
agent_test: Agent loop: LLM step then tool call (python, solver) at fixed token budget vs LLM-only.

claim: Checker feedback loops beat independent sampling inside formal proving at equal query counts (COPRA 60 queries 26.63 vs 15.98 for 60 independent few-shot samples; Goedel-V2 pass@32 with 5 revision rounds 92.7 vs 92.2 at pass@8192 without), but outside proofs at equal token budget the gain is about zero (Olausson: 1.05x and 0.97x of pass@20 and pass@22 on APPS with GPT-4), and it depends on feedback quality (own feedback 33.3 vs expert human 52.6 repaired).
agent_test: Compare k independent samples vs k-round verify-and-repair at equal total tokens on code with tests and on algebra with a symbolic check; split budget (most to first attempts, a few to repair) as Olausson suggests.

claim: Context and retrieval matter more than scale: Baldur 62b only +0.4 over 8b with context; LeanDojo retrieval 51.2 vs 47.6; GPT-f 1.5B no gain over 700M; Rango retrieval +47% relative.
agent_test: Equal-token test: add retrieved relevant prior notes vs spend the same tokens on a longer reasoning budget.

claim: Training on non-formal data or auxiliary tasks helps formal provers (GPT-f WebMath 31.58 to 42.56 at 700m; PACT 32 to 48.4 with co-training).
agent_test: Not applicable to a scaffold-only agent.

claim: Informal-to-formal drafting helps: DSP lifts miniF2F-test from 20.9 (Sledgehammer+heuristics) to 39.3 (human drafts) and 38.9 (LLM drafts); removing informal proofs costs 3.7 valid / 5.3 test. Lyra (other group, GPT-4) reproduces the level: 38.9 with GPT-4 drafts, 39.7 with human drafts at 100 attempts. The informal draft itself adds little on top of retrieval in COPRA (+0.83: 29.09 to 29.92). No 2025 reasoning-model drafter was tested in this series.
agent_test: Draft-then-check (plan in prose, convert to checkable steps) vs direct answer at equal tokens. One lab's pipeline; no independent replication seen.

claim: Bigger informal-draft writers did not help DSP in one table (Minerva test 36.5, 34.0, 30.3 for 8B/62B/540B) while another reading gives 36.5/37.7/38.9; the size effect is not established.
agent_test: Vary drafter strength in our agent holding the checker fixed.

claim: Gains do not transfer across libraries or splits: Metamath GPT-f 56.22 in-library vs 1.3 pass@1 on miniF2F; ReProver 51.2 random vs 26.3 novel-premises; PACT temporal hold-out 37.1 to 45.6 vs 48.4.
agent_test: Evaluate the agent on held-out task families, never the family used to tune the prompt.

claim: Benchmark inflation and tooling error: miniF2F saturated (Seed-Prover 99.6, Hilbert 99.2) while PutnamBench went from about 1/640 in 2024 to 331/657 and 462/660 in 2025; lean-gym misjudged 21.1% of correct proofs; at least 20% of autoformalized statements were flawed. Note: 52.94/68.85/77.87/80.74 are Kimina-Prover Preview 72B numbers; DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B is 61.9/82.4/86.6/88.9 at pass@1/32/1024/8192. 118 of 371 (31.8%) of the Lean 4 ProofNet ports had formalization errors.
agent_test: Audit our verifier for false negatives on known-good answers before trusting a score.

claim: Test-time scaling: pass rate rises with samples and search width (GPT-f width 42.90 to 56.50; DeepSeek-Prover V1 30.03 greedy to 50.0 at 65,536 samples; V2 88.9 at pass@8192) with diminishing returns per doubling (+4.39 falling to +2.45).
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs tokens for best-of-N with checker vs without; fit the per-doubling gain.

claim: Search with learned value and online training improves provers (HTPS Metamath 65.4 vs 56.5; 82.6 cumulative with online training; miniF2F-test 41.0 pass@64 vs 36.6).
agent_test: All evidence is one paper; not directly testable on a scaffold.

claim: Decomposition into lemmas and subgoals plus an informal reasoning model drives the 2025 jumps (DeepSeek-Prover-V2 88.9 miniF2F and 47/658 Putnam; Seed-Prover 331/657; Hilbert 462/660). Size at equal tokens is not isolated: DeepSeek-V2 CoT pass@32 (82.4, about 216k output tokens) beats non-CoT pass@1024 (76.7, about 780k) by our arithmetic, and Hilbert D=0 pass@4 75 vs D=3 98.7 spends millions of tokens. The reasoner model dominates: Hilbert with gpt-oss-120b 13.3 vs Gemini 2.5 Pro 70.0 on PutnamBench.
agent_test: Compare flat vs lemma-decomposed reasoning on long problems at equal tokens.

claim: Tool-integrated assistance cuts manual effort: Lean Copilot automates 74.2% of steps vs 40.1% for AESOP; manual tactics 2.08 vs 3.86.
agent_test: One paper reported twice; no user study.

claim: General LLMs without proof-specific training score near zero on hard formal tasks (GPT-4 1/640 PutnamBench; 29.0 vs 51.2 on LeanDojo; 13.52 few-shot on miniF2F).
agent_test: Baseline expectation: a prompt-only agent should not be expected to match specialized provers.

claim: Proof engineering effort is large and roughly linear in proof size (seL4 about 20 person-years and 480,000 lines; nine-project linear fit).
agent_test: Background only; abstract-level evidence.

claim: Checker escape hatches inflate results: sorry, oops and timeouts must count as failure (Selene); a Lean apply? bug passed a hidden sorry in 3 claimed DeepSeek-Prover-V2 7B proofs (1 miniF2F, 2 PutnamBench); a statement audit found 398 certified faulty items over 13 benchmark variants; flawed formalization can both inflate (weakened statements) and deflate (unprovable items) scores.
agent_test: Make the agent verifier reject vacuous passes (empty check, always-true test) and measure how often they occur.

claim: The clash is resolved: 52.94 / 68.85 / 77.87 / 80.74 (pass@1, 32, 1024, 8192 on miniF2F-test) belong to Kimina-Prover Preview 72B. DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B CoT scores 61.9 / 82.4 / 86.6 / 88.9 and cites the Kimina row in its Table 1.
agent_test: Use these in any citation; no agent test.

claim: False verifications in 2025 provers are documented but small in the open audit (3 proofs via the apply? bug in DeepSeek-Prover-V2 7B output) and no audit of Seed-Prover or Hilbert outputs exists; the larger risk is the statement, not the proof.
agent_test: Our verifier forbids axioms and sorry, re-checks with a second tool, and counts vacuous passes.

claim: Feedback quality limits repair: a model's own explanation of its error repairs 33.3% of programs vs 52.6% with an expert human explanation; removing compiler error text lowers Goedel-V2 correction accuracy.
agent_test: Give the repair step the raw checker output; compare to a self-critique-only repair at equal tokens.

claim: Failure taxonomy (PALM, GPT-3.5, Coq, 520 errors): wrong theorem application 49.6%, invalid reference 15.2%, incorrect rewrite 11.7%, redundant introductions 10.8%, tactic misuse 8.5%, bullet misuse 3.7%. Backtracking is the biggest scaffold-only gain (6.5% to 40.4%); each rule-based repair adds 3.0-6.9%.
agent_test: Log which category our agent's failed steps fall in; test backtracking and premise retrieval first.

claim: Retrieving similar earlier proofs or verified lemmas is a large in-domain lever: Rango +47% over no proof retriever (22.2 to 32.0 on 500 theorems), LEGO-Prover skill library 47.1 to 50.4, Hilbert retrieval cuts reasoner tokens 4.0M to 2.3M. Transfer to non-formal memory is untested.
agent_test: Equal-token test: add retrieved solved cases with checker-verified answers vs no memory.

claim: Contamination evidence is indirect: Putnam-AXIOM variations drop o1-preview by 19.6 points; Rango's edge over Tactician shrinks to 30.1 vs 28.3 on post-cutoff projects; Seed-Prover scores 81.8 on MiniCTX-v2 (post-Nov 2024). No Lean prover has a published variant-test.
agent_test: Evaluate the agent on post-cutoff or perturbed variants of public tasks.

claim: LLM judges used to audit formal statements have high recall and low precision (Sonnet 4.5 recall 0.82, precision 0.30; GPT-5.2 recall 0.91, precision 0.24), so they work as a screen, not a verdict.
agent_test: Use the model as a high-recall flagger; send flags to an executable or human check.

claim: Expert proof-writing telemetry (N=8, F* and Verus): spec-first planners succeed more and faster; sessions with 0-4 open errors did better than those with more than 15. No LLM-copilot user study found.
agent_test: Plan first, split goals, keep few open errors; user-study gap remains open.
